_comment: Capital-city flag files VERIFIED NOT to be that capital city's own flag — a district's, a traditional chiefdom's or another neighbouring entity's flag, a design no source documents for the city where the city's documented flag differs, or a flag recorded as superseded, that Wikidata P41, an infobox or an earlier manifest attached to the capital. build-capital-details.mjs drops these (so the P41 pass, a curated override or a preserved manifest entry can never re-add them), backfill-capital-flags.mjs never proposes them, and check-capital-flags.mjs fails the build if the manifest maps a code to one. Each entry cites the evidence. See docs/SUBNATIONAL_FLAG_AUDIT_2026-09.md.

MY-05.reason: Flag of the luak of Sungai Ujong, one of the nine traditional chiefdoms of Negeri Sembilan (FOTW my-n-su.html: 'Quartered black, yellow, white and green'), not of the city of Seremban. Seremban City Council's own flag is on FOTW my-05-se.html and is the MY-05 override.

MY-11.reason: Flag of Kuala Terengganu DISTRICT (the Commons file page: 'Flag of Kuala Terengganu, a district in Terengganu'; FOTW my-ter-m.html lists it among the Terengganu district flags). The city's own flag is the Kuala Terengganu City Council (MBKT) flag on the same FOTW page, which has no free file.

KR-11.reason: Flag of Jung District (Jung-gu), the district of Seoul where City Hall stands — Wikidata gives it as Seoul's P36. Seoul is a single city whose own flag is the KR-11 subdivision flag (ko.wikipedia 서울특별시기).

KR-26.reason: Flag of Yeonje District (Yeonje-gu), the district of Busan where City Hall stands — Wikidata gives it as Busan's P36. Busan's own flag is the KR-26 subdivision flag (ko.wikipedia 부산광역시기).

ID-SA.reason: Flag of Gorontalo City, the capital of Gorontalo province (ID-GO), which split from North Sulawesi in 2000. It reached North Sulawesi because Wikidata's North Sulawesi item (Q5068) also lists Gorontalo as a capital. North Sulawesi's capital is Manado, whose own flag (the city arms on white, FOTW id-sa-c.html) is the ID-SA override.

MA-01.reason: The flag of the Wilaya of Tangier (Commons: "Drapeau du Wilaya de Tanger"). FOTW's Moroccan subnational index (ma-.html) lists the wilaya flags created in 1976 separately from municipal flags, with Tanger among the wilayas; it is a province's flag, not the city's.

MA-02.reason: The flag of Kénitra Province (Commons: "Flag of Kenitra Province in Morocco", in "Flags of provinces of Morocco"). The app names MA-02's capital Oujda, a different city; Morocco's capital data mixes the 2015 region codes into the pre-2015 regions (see the audit ledger).

MA-03.reason: The flag of Fes Province (Commons: "Flag of Fes Province in Morocco", in "Flags of provinces of Morocco"), shown as the flag of Taza. It is neither Taza's flag nor a city's.

MA-05.reason: The flag of Fes Province (Commons: "Flag of Fes Province in Morocco"), shown as the flag of Beni Mellal, a different city in a different region.

MA-09.reason: The flag of Settat Province (Commons: "Flag of Settat Province in Morocco", in "Flags of provinces of Morocco"), not of the city of Settat.

MA-10.reason: The flag of Sidi Bennour, shown for Guelmim, which the app names as MA-10's capital. The two are different places.

IT-OR.reason: A plain white-and-red bicolour that no source documents for Oristano: the Commons file is a user's drawing made from the Flag of Cagliari file, with no source; FOTW has no page for the city and it.wikipedia describes no city flag. Oristano's documented symbol is the uprooted tree of Arborea.

IT-RN.reason: A plain white-and-red bicolour, drawn by a Commons user with no source. FOTW it-rn-rn.html reports Rimini's flag as white charged with the city arms (per flagsonline.it) and shows the city's gonfalone, which the comune describes as a drape in the colours of the arms, carrying them.

IT-TE.reason: A plain white-and-red bicolour with no source. Teramo's only granted symbol besides the arms is the gonfalone of DPR 11 September 2001, white with a red border and the arms (it.wikipedia Teramo); FOTW it-te-te.html shows that gonfalone and reports the older town flag as red and white with the red at the hoist, the reverse of this file.

SY-DI.reason: Wikimedia Commons records this Damascus Governorate logo flag as used until 2024, before the change of government. No later Damascus flag is documented (Commons category Flags of Damascus; FOTW sy-di.html shows only an older design), so the city is left without one.

SY-RD.reason: The same superseded Damascus Governorate flag, shown for Damascus as the capital of Rif Dimashq. Commons records it as used until 2024 and no later flag is documented.

GQ-BN.file: Former Flag of Santa Isabella City.svg
GQ-BN.reason: Commons: "Former flag of the Santa Isabella City, in the Spanish Guinea (nowadays Malabo)" — a colonial-era flag, recorded as former, uploaded as own work with no source. It is not Malabo's current flag.

ID-KT.reason: The flag of Banjarmasin (Commons: "Flag of Banjarmasin City", in "Flags of cities of Indonesia"), a city in South Kalimantan, shown as the flag of Central Kalimantan's capital. Central Kalimantan's capital is Palangka Raya (Wikidata Q14409), a different city in a different province.

IE-TA.reason: A plain blue and gold bicolour: Tipperary's GAA county colours. Commons files it in "Flags of GAA organising bodies" and "Flags of counties of Ireland", as own work with no source. It is not a flag of the town of Nenagh.

RO-BN.reason: Commons: "Flag of Beszterce in 1941" — a historical flag from the 1941 Hungarian book 'Városaink neve, címere és lobogója', sourced to FOTW ro-bistr.html#hist (its history section), from the WWII Hungarian annexation. It is not Bistrița's current flag.

RO-MM.reason: Commons: "Flag of Nagybánya in 1941" — a historical flag from the 1941 Hungarian book 'Városaink neve, címere és lobogója', sourced to FOTW ro-baiam.html#hist. It is not Baia Mare's current flag.

RO-SJ.reason: Commons: "Flag of Zilah in 1941" — a historical flag from the 1941 Hungarian book 'Városaink neve, címere és lobogója', sourced to FOTW ro-zalau.html#hist. It is not Zalău's current flag.

RO-SM.reason: Commons: "Flag of Szatmárnémeti in 1941" — a historical flag from the 1941 Hungarian book 'Városaink neve, címere és lobogója', sourced to FOTW ro-satum.html#hist. It is not Satu Mare's current flag.

RS-05.reason: Commons: "Flag of Zombor in 1941" — a historical flag from the 1941 Hungarian book 'Városaink neve, címere és lobogója', sourced to FOTW rs-sombo.html#ffl (a former flag). It is not Sombor's current flag.

EG-DK.reason: Dakahlia GOVERNORATE's 2006 flag (a white cogwheel in a yellow circle with red papyrus on green), not Mansoura's: FOTW eg-g-daq.html ("2006 flag"; capital al-Mansura). Commons names it for the governorate ("Governadorat de Daqahliya").

EG-MN.reason: Minya GOVERNORATE's flag (the bust of Nefertiti, found in the governorate), not the city of Minya's: FOTW eg-g-mny.html; the Commons title names the governorate.

EG-MT.reason: Matrouh GOVERNORATE's first (2006) flag, a white gazelle leaping on blue with a yellow trapezoid: FOTW eg-g-mat.html ("First flag"; capital Marsa Matruh). Commons names it for the governorate. Not Marsa Matruh's flag.

EG-SIN.reason: North Sinai GOVERNORATE's earlier (2006) flag, a white cogwheel quarter in ochre with a blue fish over water: FOTW eg-g-nsi.html ("Earlier flag"; main city al-Arish). Commons names it for the governorate. Not Arish's flag.

GT-JA.reason: Not Jalapa city's flag. FOTW's page for the city (gt-ja-ja.html) shows its flag as a plain red, yellow and green horizontal tricolour; this file, filed on Commons as the flag of Jalapa DEPARTMENT, puts the department arms in the centre, and the department page (gt-ja.html) itself records a previously reported wrong version.

GT-JU.reason: Not Jutiapa city's flag, and not a flag at all: the department arms in a laurel wreath with no field, filed on Commons as the flag of Jutiapa DEPARTMENT. FOTW's page for the city (gt-ju-ju.html) shows its flag as green-white-green with the arms (2014), and the department's (gt-ju.html) as white with the arms and the name.

PE-PAS.reason: The flag of Pasco PROVINCE (Commons: "Bandera Provincia de Pasco"), shown as the flag of the city of Cerro de Pasco. The city spans three districts (Chaupimarca, Yanacancha, Simón Bolívar) of a larger province; es.wikipedia's Cerro de Pasco article only reuses the province flag and the regional arms in its infobox and documents no city flag. A province's flag is not its capital city's (CLAUDE.md capital-flag rule 3a).

IE-CO.reason: County Cork's GAA county colours (red and white). FOTW ie-col.html: county flags in popular use are based on the colours of the county sports teams and represent the county. Not a flag of Cork city, whose council flag is a different design (FOTW ie-cork.html).

IE-LD.file: Flag of Longford, Tipperary & Roscommon County.svg
IE-LD.reason: A blue and gold county-colours flag that Commons files for three counties at once (Longford, Tipperary, Roscommon): the GAA county colours (FOTW ie-col.html). Not a flag of the town of Longford.

IE-LK.file: Flag of the counties of Fermanagh and Limerick.svg
IE-LK.reason: A green and white county-colours flag that Commons files for two counties (Fermanagh and Limerick): the GAA county colours (FOTW ie-col.html). Not a flag of Limerick city, whose council flag is a different design (FOTW ie-lim.html#limerick).

IE-WD.reason: County Waterford's white and blue GAA county colours (FOTW ie-col.html: county colours come from the county sports teams). Not a flag of Waterford city.

NG-FC.reason: The Abuja city logo ("ABUJA · The Heart of Nigeria") on a white field. FOTW ng-abuja.html documents Abuja's flag as a GREEN field bearing the logo with the name and motto in white. The white-field logo is not the documented flag.

NI-SJ.reason: The town hall's logo ("ALCALDIA San Carlos") on white. FOTW ni-rs-sc.html shows San Carlos's municipal flag as blue over green with the municipal arms. The logo is not the flag.

RO-TM.reason: The Commons file is the flag of Savoy. Its design, red with a white cross throughout, is also the HISTORICAL flag of Temesvár recorded in the 1941 Hungarian book 'Városaink neve, címere és lobogója' (FOTW ro-timis.html#hist), and the small banner on the tower in the city's arms (ro.wikipedia "Stema municipiului Timișoara"). No source documents it as Timișoara's flag today; the same case as the other 1941 flags removed in batch 7d.

LU-L.reason: A photograph of three flags hanging from a building, not a flag image.

IE-OY.reason: A plain blue and white bicolour, described on Commons only as "the flag of Tullamore Co. Offaly": a 2011 own-work upload with no source (the SVG is derived from it). FOTW's list of Irish county and town council flags (ie-coco.html) has none for Tullamore, and Offaly's county colours are green, white and gold (FOTW ie-lein.html). No source documents this flag.

GE-SK.reason: Not the documented flag of Gori. FOTW ge-gori.html gives Gori's flag as prescribed by Municipal Council Decree No. 29 of 18 August 2010: quartered red and blue by a red cross fimbriated white, skewed to the hoist. This file (a blue hoist triangle with a gold key) is a 2016 own-work Commons upload with no source.

GE-AB.reason: Not a documented flag. The Commons file is a November 2025 own-work drawing derived from a coat-of-arms image, and Commons itself tags it {{factual accuracy}}. FOTW has no page for a flag of Sukhumi/Sokhumi. A capital in a disputed territory needs a documented flag, not a construction.

NI-CA.reason: A plain purple, yellow and blue tricolour: Jinotepe's flag without its arms. FOTW ni-cr-ji.html (with photos of the flag in use) gives the flag as horizontally divided purple-yellow-blue with the municipal coat of arms in the centre. A plain field missing its arms is not the documented flag (the Terni and Udine precedent, batch 6b).

MX-QUE.reason: A PROPOSAL, not the flag: Commons describes the file as "Propuesta de Bandera del Municipio de Querétaro" (a 2022 own-work drawing) and tags it {{fictitious flag}}. FOTW mx-qt-qt.html reports a white desk flag with the municipal arms seen in a 2024 council photo, but no documented municipal flag this file reproduces.

UA-68.reason: The square blue flag with a gold border is Khmelnytskyi's 1997 city flag, which council decision No. 13 of 22 March 2017 made the flag (standard) of the city MAYOR. The city flag since then is 2:3 without the border (khm.gov.ua, "Символи міста"; uk.wikipedia "Прапор Хмельницького"). Replaced by "Flag of Khmelnytskyi (3-2).svg".

NI-GR.reason: Granada DEPARTMENT's previous flag (blue, white, yellow, white and red stripes with the arms), not Granada city's: Commons files it under "Flags of departments of Nicaragua", and FOTW ni-gr.html shows it as the department's previous flag, replaced in 2019 by a white flag with the arms. FOTW's page for the city (ni-gr-gr.html) shows the city flag as white with the city arms.

PE-LIM.reason: Not a documented flag. The Commons file ("Bandera de Huacho") is an undated own-work upload with no source; es.wikipedia's Huacho article documents only the 1964 coat of arms (section "Símbolos de Huacho"), FOTW has no page for Huacho or Huaura, and a web search found no municipal source for a flag.

PY-11.reason: Not a documented flag. The Commons file ("Bandera Municipalidad de Areguá") is a 2012 own-work upload with no source; FOTW's list of Central department subdivisions (py-11-.html) names Areguá District with no flag, es.wikipedia's Areguá article shows it in the infobox only, and a web search found no municipal source.

GT-PE.reason: Own work (Commons, 2006) with no source. FOTW's Flores page (gt-pe-fl.html) shows only the town's arms and no flag, and no other source documents one. The file's green, white and sky-blue field is Petén DEPARTMENT's tricolour (Agreement 3-98 of 1998) with the old Flores arms in place of the departmental map emblem.

GT-SM.reason: Own work (Commons, 2015, PD-shape): a plain vertical green-yellow-red triband. FOTW's San Marcos page (gt-sm-sm.html, 2011) gives the city's flag as vertical red-yellow-green with the lion's head and the city's name on the yellow, so the file lacks the emblem and reverses the colours.

GT-HU.reason: The white flag with red and yellow rectangles that Flagmaster 45 (1984) reported as Huehuetenango's (FOTW gt-hu.html). Since 1987 the 1955 Mackepeace flag, green and yellow with a hoist triangle and the Zaculeu ruins, has been the official symbol of both the municipality and the department (mihuehue.com; FOTW gt-hu-hu.html, from Prensa Libre, 31 December 2006). The GT-HU override is that flag.

GT-QZ.reason: Own work (Commons, 2012) with no source: a plain blue-white-red horizontal tricolour. FOTW's Quetzaltenango city page (gt-qz-qz.html) says the city uses the same symbols as the department, whose flag carries the arms on the white (gt-qz.html). The GT-QZ override is the department's flag.
